source: Cambodia Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries (MAFF), "ប្រព័ន្ធវប្បកម្មដំណាំស្រូវ តាមគោលការណ៍ធម្មជាតិ (ប.វ.ស)" [System of Rice Intensification Following Natural Principles / SRI], 14-page Khmer-language handout/booklet, undated, no author or elibrary URL visible on any page (footer reads "កំរណ៉ការអភិវ័ទ្ធន៍វិស្ស័យកសិកម្ម ខែត្តកំពងចាម" = "Agricultural Extension/Skills Development Office, Kampong Cham province")
text:
Nursery bed site selection (per the source document): the site should allow easy water drainage; be easy to protect from livestock and birds; have soil that is already fertile; and be positioned appropriately relative to the field to be planted.

Area needed: for 1 hectare of field to be transplanted, only about 150-200 m2 of nursery bed area is needed. Well-decomposed natural/organic fertilizer should be applied generously, and the bed should be built as small raised beds about 1.5-2 m wide, with length adjusted to the size of the field, to make sowing, irrigation, drainage, weeding, and pest control easier.

Nursery bed soil and fertilizer preparation: plow the bed soil to a depth of roughly 15 cm (described in the source as about a hand-span deep -- this depth-to-hand-span equivalence is the source's own description, recorded as given); sun-dry the plowed soil for 7-10 days before building the final bed; then apply well-decomposed animal manure or compost to the bed at a rate of about 1-2 cart-loads per 100 m2 of bed.

Seed soaking and incubation: use good quality seed at a rate of 10-15 kg per hectare of field to be planted (this rate is notably lower than typical broadcast-seeding rates used in non-SRI rice cultivation, because SRI transplants sparse, single seedlings per hill rather than broadcasting dense seed directly -- this is a characteristic feature of the SRI method itself, not a contradiction of the direct-seeding rates recorded elsewhere in the existing knowledge base). Soak seed in water for 24 hours, then wash the soaked seed clean. Spread the washed seed in a thin layer, 10-15 cm thick, in a shaded location, and cover it to help retain heat and encourage even germination. After about 12 hours, remove the cover and lightly sprinkle the seed with water.

Sowing: sow seed evenly onto the nursery bed at a rate of about 100 grams per m2. Sow in the late afternoon/evening to avoid heat damage to the newly sown seed from direct sun. If it is raining, delay sowing until the rain stops, so that seed is not washed away by rainwater.
